title: What the Node Eats
passages:
The screen on reader two blinked green, then held. The figure at the reader did not move. One glove had tape wrapped across the knuckles, white and crinkled. No name came. No badge number was spoken, though the machine had just printed one: 2244.

Teodoro wiped his hands on a rag that was already too greasy to help. "Ivo's got two cartridges left," he said. "Six more cases on the 7-K if the line holds. You want the shop log, it's behind the cathode. You want Marlowe, he's on the couch. He can't walk yet."

The figure's voice was dry, like air leaking from a worn seal. "A claim can be acknowledged by any reader. A listed man is only released off the plate by his own receiving countersign. Those are the collection rules. You know them."

"I know them," Teodoro said. "I signed the plate myself. Marlowe's crew now."

The figure turned. The shop light caught the tape on the knuckles, nothing else. "Who patched the diaphragm with glove rubber?"

Teodoro opened his mouth, then closed it. Rhea stopped pumping. The bellows of the respirator hung halfway inflated, tethered to Ivo's face by a strap and hope.

"That's not your board," Teodoro said.

"The board doesn't answer questions. People do." The figure stepped back from reader two. "Ivo's diaphragm was patched with a disc of heavy glove rubber. I want the name."

"Rhea," Teodoro said. He looked at her. "Rhea patched it. Her brother. She's been hand-pumping him for two days."

Rhea did not look up from the rubber bulb in her hands. "And I've got one more cartridge after this one. Unless you're carrying spares in that coat, you can take your rules and go back up the ore stub where you came from."

The figure did not flinch. "The cartridges are on the 7-K. They'll arrive when the compressor priority trips. The question was who patched the diaphragm, not who's breathing because of it."

"That's Rhea too," Teodoro said. He was talking too fast, he knew it, but he could not stop. It was his flaw, and Marlowe would have said so if he were awake. Marlowe was awake enough to listen from the couch, eyes open, saying nothing.

The figure turned toward the shop door. "A listed man stays listed until he countersigns himself off. Marlowe knows that now. Tell him the reclamation unit does not care about his bunk."

Then the figure walked out into the ore stub, boots crunching on the gravel grade, and did not look back.

Rhea let the pump handle fall. "Who was that?"

Teodoro shook his head. "No name. No clearance. Just badge 2244 on a reader that does not issue badges."

"Two cartridges," Rhea said. She squeezed the bulb again, soft and mechanical. Ivo's chest rose. "Tell me that was enough."

Teodoro looked at reader two, where the green light was still holding. "He's gone up the ore stub. Nobody here can say how a stranger knew about glove rubber, or which brother was dying."

Rhea did not stop pumping. She kept her hand on the bulb, watching the door. "If someone was standing four feet from Marlowe's couch and knew about the patch, they've been inside this shop. They've been listening."

"Then they left," Teodoro said. He did not sound sure. "And they took their name with them."
